emails.subject: CSE 2050-001-1268: Announcement - HW 4 deadline extended
emails.body:
CSE 2050 - Data Structures and Object-Oriented Design (Section 001)
Announcement posted by Daniel Okafor

Hi everyone,

A lot of you came to office hours today stuck on the same part of Homework 4 (the recursive merge in Part C), and after looking at the autograder logs I think the spec was genuinely unclear about how to handle empty lists. That's on me. I have posted a corrected spec (v2) under Course Content > Homework > HW 4.

Because of that, I am extending the Homework 4 deadline. It was originally due tomorrow, Friday 10/9, at 11:59 PM. It is now due Tuesday, October 13 at 11:59 PM on Gradescope. If you already submitted, you do not need to resubmit unless your Part C tests are failing. The autograder has been rerun against the corrected tests.

Two things that are NOT changing:

1. Lab 6 (Linked Lists) is still due Saturday at 11:59 PM as usual. Labs are graded on completion, so please just get it in.

2. The midterm is still Wednesday, October 21, 6:30-8:30 PM in ITE C80. This is a common exam for all sections, so it is not during our normal lecture time. Bring your UConn ID. If you have a conflict with another common exam, email me by end of day Wednesday 10/14 so I can arrange a makeup. I cannot accommodate requests after that.

A practice midterm will go up on HuskyCT this weekend.

See you Monday,
Prof. Okafor

--
Daniel Okafor, Ph.D.
Assistant Professor in Residence
School of Computing
University of Connecticut
Office hours: Tue/Thu 2:00-3:30 PM, ITE 259

emails.subject: Engineering Undergraduate Weekly | October 5, 2026
emails.body:
ENGINEERING UNDERGRADUATE WEEKLY
News, opportunities, and reminders for UConn Engineering students
Week of October 5, 2026

==================================================
IN THIS ISSUE
- A note from the Associate Dean
- Research spotlight: Senior design team heads to nationals
- Career corner
- Around campus
- Notes & reminders
- Tutoring and support
==================================================

A NOTE FROM THE ASSOCIATE DEAN

Dear students,

It is hard to believe we are already at the midpoint of the semester. The leaves on Horsebarn Hill are turning, the line at the Dairy Bar is finally manageable, and the library is filling up, which can only mean one thing: midterms. I want to remind you that this stretch of the semester is hard for everyone, including the students who look like they have it all figured out. Use your resources. Go to office hours. Sleep.

I also want to thank the more than 400 of you who came out to the Engineering Welcome Back Picnic last month. It was our largest turnout in a decade, and we ran out of burgers in 40 minutes. We have taken note.

With warm regards,
Dr. Elena Marchetti
Associate Dean for Undergraduate Education

--------------------------------------------------
RESEARCH SPOTLIGHT: SENIOR DESIGN TEAM HEADS TO NATIONALS

A team of four mechanical engineering seniors has been selected as one of twelve national finalists in the ASME Student Design Competition for their low-cost, solar-powered water purification unit. The team, advised by Prof. Ravi Subramanian, spent last spring and summer iterating on a prototype that can produce 40 liters of drinkable water per day for under $90 in parts.

"We broke it about fifteen times," said team lead Hannah Kowalczyk '27. "Honestly that was the most useful part."

The team will present in Portland, Oregon in November. Read the full story on the College of Engineering news site.

--------------------------------------------------
CAREER CORNER

Thank you to everyone who attended the Fall Engineering Career Fair in Gampel Pavilion. More than 180 employers attended this year. If you collected business cards, the Center for Career Readiness and Life Skills recommends sending a short follow-up note within two weeks.

Did not find what you were looking for? Handshake currently lists over 600 internship postings open to engineering majors, and many summer 2027 roles are still being posted. Drop-in resume reviews are available at the Career Center in Wilbur Cross, Monday through Thursday, 12:00 to 4:00 PM. No appointment is needed.

Employers recruiting on campus this month include Pratt & Whitney, Electric Boat, Collins Aerospace, Medtronic, and Eversource. See Handshake for information session times.

--------------------------------------------------
AROUND CAMPUS

- First Night is back! The men's and women's basketball teams tip off the season with First Night at Gampel Pavilion on Friday, October 16. Doors open at 6:00 PM. Student tickets are free with your UConn ID, first come, first served.

- The Homer Babbidge Library will be open 24 hours beginning Sunday, October 11 through the end of midterm season. The Bookworms Cafe will keep its normal hours.

- Student Health and Wellness is offering free flu shots at walk-in clinics in the Student Union throughout October. Bring your UConn ID and insurance card. No appointment needed.

- Construction update: the walkway between the Engineering and Science Building and ITE will be closed for repaving through approximately October 20. Please use the Fairfield Way entrance.

--------------------------------------------------
NOTES & REMINDERS

Several of you have asked about the makerspace in the Innovation Partnership Building. Yes, it is open to all engineering undergraduates, and no, you do not need to be enrolled in a design course to use it. You do need to complete the online safety training first. Hours are posted on the door and on the IPB website. On a related note, the College's continuing student scholarship application for the 2027-28 academic year is now open in the Husky Scholarship Portal, and a single application puts you in consideration for more than 80 donor-funded awards, including several that went unawarded last year because too few students applied. The application requires one short essay (500 words) and closes Sunday, October 18 at 11:59 PM. Late applications are not accepted under any circumstances, so please do not wait until the last night. Finally, a reminder that lockers in the Castleman Building are assigned by semester, and anything left in an unregistered locker over winter break will be removed.

The Academic Calendar is always available at registrar.uconn.edu. Spring 2027 class schedules are now viewable in Student Admin.

--------------------------------------------------
TUTORING AND SUPPORT

The Engineering Tutoring Center (Engineering II, Room 315) offers free drop-in tutoring for 1000- and 2000-level engineering, math, physics, and chemistry courses.

Fall hours:
Sunday: 4:00 PM - 9:00 PM
Monday - Thursday: 11:00 AM - 9:00 PM
Friday: 11:00 AM - 3:00 PM

The Q Center (Homer Babbidge Library, Level 1) and the W Center are also available for quantitative and writing support.

If you are struggling, academically or otherwise, please reach out. Your academic advisor, the Dean of Students Office, and Student Health and Wellness - Mental Health are all here to help.

==================================================
Engineering Undergraduate Weekly is sent to all undergraduate students in the College of Engineering during the academic year. Have an item for a future issue? Email engr-undergrad@uconn.edu by Thursday at noon.

College of Engineering | University of Connecticut
261 Glenbrook Road, Unit 3237, Storrs, CT 06269

emails.subject: Spring 2027 advising - hold on your account
emails.body:
Hi Alex,

I hope your semester is going well. I'm reaching out to my advisees because Spring 2027 registration is around the corner, and I see that you have not yet scheduled your advising meeting.

As a reminder, all School of Computing students have an advising hold placed on their account each semester. I can only remove the hold after we have met. According to Student Admin, your enrollment appointment opens Monday, October 26 at 8:00 AM, so we need to meet before then. My calendar fills up quickly in the last week, so I'd strongly encourage you to grab a slot now.

To schedule: log in to Nexus (nexus.uconn.edu), choose "Schedule Appointment," and select me as your advisor. I have openings between October 12 and October 23. Appointments are 20 minutes and can be in person (ITE 250) or on Teams.

Before our meeting, please:
- Run your Academic Requirements report in Student Admin and look it over
- Fill out the Spring Course Planning Worksheet (attached) with the classes you'd like to take, plus two or three alternates
- Think about whether you want to declare a concentration. You're at the point where it starts to matter for sequencing.

If you're thinking about study abroad, a co-op, or adding a minor, let me know ahead of time so I can pull the right information.

Looking forward to catching up.

Best,
Karen

Karen Liebowitz
Academic Advisor, School of Computing
College of Engineering | University of Connecticut
ITE 250 | 860-555-0142
Pronouns: she/her
Book an appointment: nexus.uconn.edu
